terms.definition: Full collection of elements about which a question is asked.
Observed subset of a population.
Graph of cumulative relative frequency.
Arithmetic average for data; probability-weighted average for a random variable.
Middle ordered value, or average of the two middle values.
Mean squared deviation from a distribution mean; sample estimation uses n−1.
Square root of variance, expressed in the original units.
Signed distance from a mean measured in standard deviations.
Third quartile minus first quartile.
A quartile shifted outward by 1.5 or 3 interquartile ranges in the course rule.
Set of possible outcomes of an experiment.
Events that cannot occur simultaneously.
Ordered selection or arrangement.
Unordered selection of distinct objects.
Probability after restricting to a given event with positive probability.
Joint event probabilities factor; for random variables, the joint distribution factors into marginals.
Probability assigned to each value of a discrete random variable.
F(x)=P(X≤x), defined for every real x.
Probability-weighted average of a random quantity, when it exists.
Number of total independent constant-p trials through the first success.
Success count in a fixed number of independent constant-p Bernoulli trials.
Number of total independent constant-p trials through the rth success.
Success count in simple random sampling without replacement from a finite population.
Nonnegative-integer count distribution with equal mean and variance λ.
Density whose area over a region gives probability.
β in the course gamma distribution; mean is αβ.
Continuous waiting-time model with mean equal to scale β.
Symmetric bell-shaped model N(μ,σ²).
Distribution-free lower bound on probability near the mean, assuming finite variance.
E[exp(tX)]; derivatives at zero yield moments when it exists near zero.
Distribution of one variable obtained by summing/integrating out the others.
Expected product of centered variables.
Covariance divided by the product of nonzero standard deviations.
Fit that minimizes the sum of squared observed-minus-predicted responses.
Fraction of observed response variation accounted for by a simple least-squares fit with intercept.
Random sample-based rule for estimating a parameter.
Observed numerical value of an estimator.
Expected estimator minus the parameter being estimated.
Standard deviation of an estimator’s sampling distribution.
Independent and identically distributed.
Probability distribution of a statistic across repeated samples under a specified model.
